evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.53: C. Marius … cum secārētur
Traupman 169, 354, 388: chīrurgus eam secuit, the surgeon operated on her
terms.comment: To have an operation is to be cut: secārī. The surgeon is chīrurgus (Traupman 169; Greek χειρουργός).

phrases.latin: C. Marius, rūsticānus vir, sed plānē vir, cum secārētur, ut suprā dīxī, prīncipiō vetuit sē alligārī
phrases.english: Gaius Marius, a countryman but every inch a man, when he was being operated on, as I said above, at first refused to be tied down

phrases.latin: nec quisquam ante Marium solūtus dīcitur esse sectus
phrases.english: and no one before Marius is said to have been operated on without being tied down
